newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico retail recovery not seen until 2001 - ANTAD.
newsitem.headline: Mexico retail recovery not seen until 2001 - ANTAD.

text.p: Mexico's National Department Store Association (ANTAD) predicted the retail sector will not recover to 1994 pre-peso devaluation levels until 2001.

"The recovery to 1994 sales levels in real terms will be achieved in self-service stores in 2001...and in department stores in 2003," ANTAD president Luis Santana Castillo told a news conference late Thursday.
The recovery rides on an expected annual sales recovery of five percent annually beginning in 1998, he added.
Santana said the sharp drops in consumption in the past two years should end in 1997.

"The primary objective is to not continue falling. We expect to begin the year with drops in sales and end the year with a sales recovery," he said, adding that annual sales in real terms in 1997 should be the same as in 1996.
ANTAD figures show sales at self-service stores fell 15.8 percent in 1995 and 8.6 percent in 1996.
